project: Yoga Pose Classification with Cross-Modal Attention Keypoint Encoder
evaluation_note: On a 157-sample test set with 5 balanced classes, a 2-point accuracy gap corresponds to approximately 3 misclassified samples — not statistically significant.

models.name: Baseline MLP
models.notes: Strong baseline; flattened keypoints with ReLU and dropout

models.name: Cross-Modal (original, target sweep)
models.architecture: Embed → SA(2 layers, 2 heads) → CA(2 layers) → MeanPool → FC(64) → 5
models.notes: Original architecture from target sweep. Strong validation but lower test generalization.

models.name: Cross-Modal + Skip + MeanMax
models.architecture: Embed → SA(2 layers, 4 heads) → CA(2 layers) → MeanMaxPool + RawSkip → FC(128) → 5
models.notes: Added raw keypoint skip connection and mean+max pooling. Slightly improved over original.

models.name: Cross-Modal (no SA, flatten raw)
models.architecture: Embed → CA(2 layers) → MeanMaxPool + FlattenRaw(68) → FC(128/64) → 5
models.notes: Removed self-attention, added flattened raw keypoint skip. Good efficiency.

models.name: Cross-Modal (no SA, no skip)
models.notes: Highest validation among variants (90.38%) but lower test (85.99%).

models.name: Cross-Modal + SA + Flatten Raw (best test)
models.architecture: Embed → SA(2 layers, 4 heads) → CA(2 layers) → MeanMaxPool + FlattenRaw(68) → FC(128/64) → 5
models.notes: Best cross-modal test accuracy (88.54%). Full architecture with raw flatten and bs=64, dropout=0.2.

models.name: Cross-Modal (pure SA, no CA bridge)
models.architecture: Embed → SA(2 layers, 4 heads) → FlattenRaw → FC(128/64) → 5
models.notes: Removed cross-modal bridge entirely. Good validation but poor test.

test_time_augmentation.note: Averaging predictions over 5 augmented views improves by 0.63 points over single-view (88.54%)

baseline_plus_flat.note: Equal-weight ensemble of Baseline MLP and Cross-Modal flat

stacked_validation_optimal.note: Grid-searched on validation set; optimal weight prefers cross-modal alone

key_findings: Cross-Modal + Self-Attention achieves higher validation accuracy (89.74%) than Baseline MLP (88.46%)
Baseline MLP generalizes better to the test set (90.45% vs 88.54% for best cross-modal)
The 2-point test gap (~3 samples on 157 test images) is within statistical noise
Self-attention improves validation but can hurt test generalization on this small dataset
Flattened raw keypoint skip connections improve cross-modal test performance by ~1 point
All models train in under 1 minute on Apple Silicon MPS
Cross-modal attention provides interpretability (attention maps, gradient analysis) that MLP cannot
